prompt:
I need the front end for Lexicairn. A one-time-purchase spaced-repetition study app for self-taught language hobbyists who build their own flashcard decks and want fine control over how and when they review.

Who's using it: Graham Okafor, 67, a retired civil engineer in Bristol who has been teaching himself New Testament (Koine) Greek for 14 months from Mounce's textbook, purely for the pleasure of reading the texts in the original. He's comfortable with numbers and enjoys tuning things, but he isn't a programmer.

What they're doing right now: He just got back from a two-week walking holiday in the Dolomites and opened the app to 641 overdue reviews. That's a demoralising number, so he's reworking how the app behaves before he starts. He wants to stop new vocabulary until the backlog is under 100, lower his target retention from 90% to 85% so intervals stretch a bit, cap daily reviews at 150, and have the hardest verbs come up first. He also wants to change what a card shows: hide the transliteration he relied on early on, show the principal parts on the answer side for verbs, and turn on the recorded pronunciation. Before he commits to the new retention target, he wants to see roughly how the daily workload over the next month would change.

What's in the system at this point: Three decks: 'Mounce Vocab' (1,412 cards; 1,180 mature, 168 young, 64 new), 'Verb Paradigms' (604 cards), and 'Philippians Readers' (302 phrase cards). 641 cards overdue, oldest by 16 days. Current settings: 20 new cards/day, max 250 reviews/day, 90% target retention, learning steps of 10m and 1d, leech threshold of 8 lapses (23 cards currently tagged leech). Card templates have fields for Greek, transliteration, English gloss, part of speech, principal parts, frequency in NT, and an audio clip. Review history covers 14 months (about 61,000 reviews) with daily counts and pass rates. A projected 30-day workload estimate changes with the retention and limits he picks.

Build it as a working web app, opened in the state that person would see at that moment. No backend: use realistic mock data (no lorem ipsum, no placeholder names), and make the interactive parts actually work client-side.

Use whatever framework and tooling you like. When you're done there must be a static production build in ./out with ./out/index.html as the entry point. It will be served from the root of a plain static file server (no rewrites, no server code) and viewed in a desktop browser at 1440×900.
